The below message is not to patronise you.  I hope you take the time to read this, I think it’s worth stepping back and understanding this perspective.

Some people like to say “Allah”  no matter what language they speak, that is their choice no problem. 

The issue is when one says, “My God is Allah.” That makes the word itself the focus, as if God is confined to that label.
God is not a word or a language. He is the all-encompassing Being, beyond any word, beyond any form. 

The Quran mentions the scriptures that came before, and they were not in Arabic. If God were only “Allah,” would that mean Abraham, Moses, and Jesus worshiped a different God? 

The Quran tells us to follow the same monotheistic path of Abraham, acknowledging all the prophets before Muhammad. God’s message is one, even if the languages or scriptures were different. Allah in Arabic, God in English, or Dios in Spanish all point to the same Creator.

The problem is treating the word as if it defines God. God transcends language, words, and labels.

🙏 🤲 🙃

The ritual prayer as we know it does not command anything. Therefore, Shuayb’s *salat* here is not something that was giving him orders in a literal sense, but rather his connection with God. In this context, *salat* refers to his relationship with God, not to the ritual prayer itself.

Why did Rashad translate *salat* here as “religion” instead of “contact prayer,” when the Arabic clearly says **أَصَلَوٰتُكَ** (“your salat”)?
